Coordinates as columns

Source: R/convert.R
geo_coords.Rd

geo_coords() gives one row per vertex, with the CRS and edge type as the attributes crs and edges, which geo_from_coords() takes back: x, y, and z and m when present, with feature (the element of x), part (the simple geometry within a multi-geometry or collection) and ring (the polygon ring, NA outside polygons). Null and empty geometries have no rows. geo_from_coords() is the reverse for one native type, and geo_points() makes points straight from vectors (design section 6.10).

Usage

geo_coords(x)

geo_from_coords(
  coords,
  type,
  n = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  edges = NULL,
  layout = c("separated", "interleaved")
)

geo_points(
  x,
  y,
  z = NULL,
  m = NULL,
  crs = NULL,
  edges = NULL,
  layout = c("separated", "interleaved")
)

Arguments

x

A geo_vctr for geo_coords(); x coordinates for geo_points().

coords

A data frame with x, y, optionally z and m, and feature, part and ring as geo_coords() gives them, ordered by feature. part and ring default to 1.

type

One of "point", "linestring", "polygon", "multipoint", "multilinestring" and "multipolygon".

n

The number of features; by default the largest feature. Features with no rows are empty.

crs, edges

As for geo_vctr(); by default the crs and edges attributes of coords.

layout

As for geo_as_native().

y, z, m

Coordinate vectors; z and m may be NULL.

Value

geo_coords(): a data frame; the others: a geo_vctr.

Examples

x <- geo_vctr("POLYGON ((0 0, 1 0, 0 1, 0 0))")
geo_coords(x)
#>   x y feature part ring
#> 1 0 0       1    1    1
#> 2 1 0       1    1    1
#> 3 0 1       1    1    1
#> 4 0 0       1    1    1
geo_points(1:3, 4:6)
#> <geo_vctr[3] geoarrow.point native, xy, separated; crs none; edges planar>
#> [1] POINT (1 4)
#> [2] POINT (2 5)
#> [3] POINT (3 6)
